gaps.wanted: A drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. Neither staged document draws any of them flat: the quick start's mounting figures show the lid and one side in three-quarter view while brackets are being screwed on, which is enough to see that nothing is printed or punched there and not enough to model. Each of the four therefore carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked, per docs/deliberately-empty-faces.md - EMPTY BY VERIFICATION, not by omission. L45 STILL WARNS ABOUT THEM AND THIS GAP IS WHAT ANSWERS IT, because that rule exempts a view a gap names rather than one carrying an `empty:` sentence. Worth saying plainly: the CSR440 clears the same rule only because an unrelated chassis-weight gap happens to scope all six views, which the rule's own comment calls over-exemption; this one names the four faces because they are what it is about. IT DOES NOT COST THE DEVICE ITS CAPABILITY LEVEL. I asserted that it did and was wrong - the grader reads six views here and the 3D build is whole. A mechanical drawing would still improve these four faces from honest blanks to drawn ones.

What the last two white legend boxes say. The label strip carries six bracketed groups of four - the breakout lane legend, one bracket per QSFP28 port, and they read 49 to 54 in order - and then TWO MORE boxes of the same size and pitch at 362.98 and 369.01 mm, under the numerals for ports 47 and 48, belonging to no bracket. At 5 px/mm their contents are not legible and no table in either document accounts for a seventh pair. They are left undrawn rather than guessed, and this gap is the record that they exist and where.

An orthographic elevation, or a mechanical drawing. The only full-panel figures this corpus holds are perspective renders: the top cover is drawn above the face and the face tapers 0.9% from its top edge to its bottom. That costs the vertical axis entirely - every y on both faces is constructed from the registry's row pitch and the family's idiom rather than read - and it leaves the horizontal axis with a 0.84% residual against the stated width, which is why the panel is 442.5 because two documents say so rather than because the drawing shows it. A flat elevation would settle the row positions, the label-strip height and the width residual in one pass.

A way to print a numeral and its direction arrow together. Each of the 48 SFP+ numerals is drawn on the metal as a digit followed by a small up or down triangle - "1 up", "2 down" - naming which row of the column the port is in. Block expansion generates the digit and has no vocabulary for the glyph beside it, and hand-writing 48 marks to add it would take the whole block out of generation for one triangle each. The digits are generated and the arrows are not; the row is unambiguous from the numeral's own side of the column centre, which is measured and correct.

The positions of the four QSFP28 breakout windows. The guide's Port LEDs table says each QSFP28 port shows "1-4 LEDs Amber (25G breakout)" and "1-4 LEDs Purple (10G breakout)", so there are four windows per cage, and the art at 5 px/mm shows a row of dots inside each cage's bezel band without resolving where they sit. One lamp per port is drawn, carrying all four vocabularies as states - the same choice edgecore/as5912-54x made on the same cluster. Four windows at invented positions would be a claim about metal this figure cannot support.

An elevation of the DC supply. The rear elevation draws the AC pair; the DC variant appears only in the small three-quarter "DC Power" figure on page 2, which shows the green three-pole pluggable terminal and the bail handle clearly enough to know what is there and not clearly enough to measure it. edgecore/dcs201-psu-dc@1 therefore borrows its face size from the AC supply, which fills the same bay, and marks every element position estimated.

What each fan module prints beside its airflow diamond. Every one of the five carries a diamond mark in its upper right corner, and at 5 px/mm the characters next to it are not legible. The convention across this vendor is an F2B or B2F legend that follows the airflow variant, and that is what is drawn, from common/fan-module@1's field of the same name; the DCS201's own art neither confirms nor contradicts it.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory`; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in a missing `attrs.power` section (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow-colour-convention.note: THE DEVICE'S OWN GUIDE SAYS IT, which matters because roc-ops/Portrayal#277 is open against two chassis that painted a back-to-front build in the front-to-back colours. Page 1, Airflow Reversal, verbatim: "1. F2B Airflow - Remove front-to-back (F2B) airflow fan trays (red handles) and PSUs (red release latches)." and "2. B2F Airflow - Install back-to-front (B2F) airflow fan trays (blue handles) and PSUs (blue release latches)." Both b2f configurations below therefore override every handle, latch and airflow legend, and the quotation is on the configuration rather than in a comment.

gate-1.note: THE ASPECT TEST FAILS, AND THE REASON IS IDENTIFIED. The front elevation on page 1, rendered from the PDF page at 600 dpi, gives a face 2222 px wide by 204 px tall - an aspect of 10.89 against the stated 442.5 / 43.95 = 10.07, which is 8.2% out and past the 4% gate. IT IS A PERSPECTIVE RENDER, NOT AN ELEVATION: the top cover is drawn as a visible trapezoid above the face, and the face itself TAPERS, reading 2228 px wide at the top row of cages and 2208 px at the bottom of the label strip. A drawing whose width depends on the height it is measured at is not an orthographic projection, and its vertical axis carries no scale. SO THE TWO AXES ARE TREATED DIFFERENTLY BELOW, and which is which is stated on every number.

how-many-management-jacks.note: THE TWO DOCUMENTS DISAGREE AND THE DRAWING SETTLES IT. The quick start's front callout reads "2 x 1000BASE-T RJ-45 management ports" and its elevation draws two jacks stacked in one bezel at the left of the face. The datasheet's Supported Transceivers and Cables section lists "1 x RJ-45 100/1000BASE-T management" - one, not two, and at a different speed pair. TWO IS MODELLED, because the callout and the picture agree with each other against a single line in a table about transceivers, and because the elevation resolves two openings at 5 px/mm with a measured 12 mm pitch between them. The datasheet line is recorded here rather than dismissed: if it is right, this face has one jack and a blank, and what would settle it is a photograph of the left end square on.

lamps.note: quick start, System LEDs/Buttons and Port LEDs, verbatim. System: "PS1/PS2: Green (OK), Amber (fault)", "OS Diag: Green (OK), Amber (fault)", "Fan: Green (OK), Amber (fault)", "Loc: Flashing Amber (switch locator)", and a "Reset Button" beside them. Ports: "SFP+ LEDs: Green (10G), Amber (1G)", "MGMT LEDs: Green (1G)", "QSFP28 LEDs: 1 LED Green (100G), 1 LED Blue (40G), 1-4 LEDs Amber (25G breakout), 1-4 LEDs Purple (10G breakout)". THE QSFP28 ENTRY DESCRIBES A GROUP OF FOUR WINDOWS AND ONE LAMP IS DRAWN PER PORT, which is the same simplification edgecore/as5912-54x makes with six common/led-dot for six cages. The breakout colours are carried as states on that one lamp rather than four windows being invented at positions the art does not resolve at 5 px/mm.

port-order.note: MEASURED, from the label strip at 600 dpi. Each column prints TWO numerals side by side on one baseline - the odd number left of centre with an up arrow, the even number right of it with a down arrow: "1 2 3 4 5 6 ..." reading across, but "1" and "2" both belonging to the first column. The first four centre at 29.0, 37.1, 42.8 and 50.3 mm against column centres of 32.75 and 47.00, so each pair straddles its own column's centre. Ports therefore run DOWN each column and then right, which is what block expansion's divmod already does, and the numerals take dx-by-row rather than dx-by-col.

power.note: datasheet and quick start: "356 Watts maximum" for the chassis. Each supply is rated 400 W output, so a single supply covers the chassis and the pair is redundant, which is what "Redundant hot-swappable AC or -48 VDC PSUs" claims.

sources.note: Two documents, both staged and both docling-converted, MEASURED OFF THE PDF PAGE RATHER THAN THE CONVERTED FIGURES. dcs201-datasheet (the DCS201 / AS5835-54X data sheet) holds the specification tables and one product shot; dcs201-qsg (the AS5835-54X Quick Start Guide) holds the panel art. The guide is the richer document by far - 108 figures - and page 1 carries the front and rear elevations, the enlarged System LED and Port LED details, the FRU replacement pictures and the airflow-reversal pair. THE GUIDE DISCLAIMS ITS OWN DRAWINGS: "The switch drawings in this document are for illustration only and may not match your particular switch model." Every number below that comes from a drawing is therefore checked against a stated figure or a registry standard before it is used, and where the two disagree it is said so rather than averaged.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 24 SFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-47/port-48). Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 2 QSFP pairs (port-49/port-50 and port-52/port-53).

the-management-lamps-are-not-on-the-jack.note: MEASURED, and it is the opposite of the usual case. docs/rj45-family-design.md reserves the lamped common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 for Ethernet jacks because nearly every Ethernet jack carries its two lamps in the bezel corners. THIS ONE DOES NOT. The label strip below the jacks prints "MGMT" between an up and a down arrow with TWO PLAIN WHITE WINDOWS beneath it at 12.24 and 21.13 mm, and "1G bps" under those, and "On = link / Flash = ACT" beside them. Those windows are the lamps - one per jack, named by the arrows - and they are 30 mm down the face, nowhere near the bezel. So the jacks take the BARE ganged part and the two lamps are placed where the metal puts them, which is also the only arrangement that does not claim two holes in the same metal.

the-management-pair-is-ganged.note: MEASURED, AND IT CHANGED THE PART. The two 1000BASE-T jacks stack at the far left with their openings centred 13.57 mm apart on the figure's own vertical scale - and two std/rj45@2 housings are 13.2 tall, which cannot stack on a 12 mm pitch without overlapping. Scaled into the constructed vertical they sit about 12.0 apart, which is std/rj45-ganged@2's measured row pitch of ~12.1 from the TE 2497310-1 CAD. So this is a 2x1 GANGED block and not two separate jacks, and it takes the ganged part.

the-qsfp-cluster.note: MEASURED IN X, CONSTRUCTED IN Y, AND HAND-WRITTEN BECAUSE THE NUMBERING SPLITS. Two columns centre at 385.30 and 404.36 mm - a 19.06 step against the registry's 19.0 ganged pitch - and each carries THREE openings, so 49/50/51 run down the left column and 52/53/54 down the right. The top two rows are one 2-high ganged shell with its numerals printed between them the way the SFP+ pairs are ("49 50" on one baseline, "52 53" on the next column's); the third row is a separate block below. A three-row block would print those numerals on three different baselines, so the six placements are written out instead.

the-rear.note: MEASURED IN X BY THE SAME RULER, and it closes on itself. The five fan grilles centre at 103.6, 162.5, 221.4, 280.1 and 338.9 mm - four steps of 58.97, 58.85, 58.77 and 58.80 - so the bay pitch is 58.8. The two supplies were read with an edge scan rather than a threshold, because a threshold on a bright module against dark chassis clips the duller edge: their frames read 16.74-71.13 and 370.78-425.37, giving 54.39 and 54.59 against the 54.0 the rest of this family's supplies measure. The fan block those centres imply runs 74.2 to 368.3, which leaves 3.5 mm to the first supply's right edge and 3.1 mm to the second's left, and margins of 16.7 and 17.1 at the two ends. Four independent quantities agreeing to a third of a millimetre is why these numbers are used rather than estimated.

the-rear-fans-are-not-the-family-part.note: FIVE, NOT SIX, AND WIDER. The three sibling chassis - AS5912-54X, AS7326-56X and AS7726-32X - each carry six common/fan-module@1 on a 48.6 pitch. This device carries five on a 58.8 pitch: the quick start's rear callout reads "5 x fan trays" and the datasheet "4+1 redundant fan modules". Five centres 235.3 mm apart cannot be six modules 48.6 apart, which would span 194.4. So the fan is its own part and the supplies, which measure 54.0, are not.

the-supplies-are-400-w.note: STATED TWICE AND IT IS WHY THEY ARE NEW PARTS. "AC PSU / Power Rating / 100-240 VAC, 50-60 Hz, 400 Watts" and "48 VDC PSU / Power Rating / 48 VDC, 400 Watts", against a chassis drawing "356 Watts maximum". common/psu-ac-650@3 and common/psu-dc-650@2 fit the bay exactly and assert 650 W, which this vendor does not claim here. A shape may be shared; a rating may not.

the-three-groups.note: MEASURED. The 24 columns are not evenly spaced: there is extra metal after the eighth and the sixteenth. Column centres 1, 9 and 17 read 32.78, 149.70 and 266.31 mm, where a plain 14.25 pitch would put 9 and 17 at 146.78 and 260.78 - so each group boundary adds about 2.84 mm. One block with gang 8 and gutter 2.84 reproduces all three groups, landing column 9 within 0.08 mm and column 17 within 0.15 mm of where they are drawn.

the-width-question.note: ANSWERED, AND IN THE DOCUMENTS' FAVOUR. The issue that scoped this device asks whether 442.5 mm quotes the body or the body plus something, because it is wider than the 438.4 the rest of the Edgecore line uses. The front view shows no ears, no flanges and nothing outboard of the chassis - the rack brackets are separate parts in the package contents - so the widest thing drawn IS the body. AND THE ARITHMETIC IS CONSISTENT WITH 442.5. Read against the registry SFP pitch the face measures 438.8 mm, which is 0.84% under the stated width. That sounds like a contradiction and is not one: the face's own taper across its height is 0.9%, the same order, so the discrepancy is inside the error of a perspective drawing and cannot be used to overturn a figure two documents state identically. Gate 1's job is to CHECK a stated dimension, not to replace it, and 0.84% passes comfortably. 442.5 x 473.3 x 43.95 is therefore taken as stated, and the residual is recorded as a gap rather than silently absorbed. THIS ANSWERS IT FOR THE SIBLING TOO. dcs202 shares this shell and the three EXP models are quoted at 442 by the same house style; none of them needs to re-open the question.

the-x-axis-is-measured.note: The horizontal axis survives, because a scale error cancels when the ruler is read at the same height as the thing measured. The ruler is the SFP+ ganged pitch: 24 columns in three groups of eight, whose within-group step reads 72.14 px, averaged over 21 steps in three independent runs that agree to 0.07 px. Against std/sfp-ganged@1's registry width of 14.25 - a lookup from SFF-8433, not a measurement - that fixes 5.0636 px/mm, and every x below is taken at that scale from the left face edge at page x 193. IT IS CONFIRMED FRONT AGAINST REAR. The rear elevation, drawn beside the front and measured by the same method, reads 2221 px across its face where the front reads 2222 - 0.05% apart. Two faces of one chassis agreeing to half a tenth of a percent is the check that the scale is the drawing's and not the measurer's.

the-y-axis-is-derived.note: NOT MEASURED, AND NOT PRETENDED TO BE. With the vertical scale unusable, the row positions come from two things that are not this drawing. The first is the registry: std/sfp-ganged@1 states a belly-to-belly row-pitch of 15.0, measured off TE 2007562-6, and the block uses it rather than the 17.0 the figure appears to show. The second is the family: edgecore/as5912-54x, the same vendor's 48x SFP+ plus 6x QSFP28 1RU leaf, puts its two rows at y 3.0 and 17.6. A top row at 3.0 with a 15.0 pitch puts the second at 18.0 and the cages' lower edge at 28.4, which leaves 15.5 mm for the label strip and the bottom vent - the proportions the drawing does show. Every y below is that construction, and none of it is a reading.
